corpus.note: Accession numbers verified against two independent SEC EDGAR endpoints (XBRL companyconcept filing dates + EDGAR browse-edgar atom feed). Use these directly with sec-edgar-downloader or the EDGAR archive URL pattern to pull the exact right filings.

questions.question: What was Apple's net income for fiscal year 2023?
What was Microsoft's net income for fiscal year 2023?
What was Walmart's net income for the fiscal year ended January 31, 2023?
What was JPMorgan Chase's net income for fiscal year 2023?
What was Apple's revenue for fiscal year 2022?
According to Apple's fiscal year 2023 income statement, what was the operating margin (operating income divided by revenue)?
questions.source_section: Item 8, Consolidated Statements of Operations table
questions.note: requires a computation across two rows of the same table, not a single stored value

questions.question: According to Microsoft's fiscal year 2023 income statement, what was the operating margin?
According to Microsoft's fiscal year 2022 income statement, what was the operating margin?
According to Apple's fiscal year 2022 income statement, what was the operating margin?
questions.source_section: Item 8, Consolidated Statements of Operations table

questions.question: What was Walmart's total net sales (revenue from contracts with customers) as reported in the fiscal year 2023 income statement table?
questions.source_section: Item 8, Consolidated Statements of Income table
questions.note: this is net sales specifically, not Walmart's total revenue figure which also includes membership and other income

questions.question: According to Apple's fiscal year 2023 Form 10-K, Item 1A Risk Factors, how does Apple describe its market share position in smartphones, personal computers and tablets?
questions.expected_answer: "The Company has a minority market share in the global smartphone, personal computer and tablet markets." (verbatim quote)
questions.note: VERIFIED verbatim quote, fetched directly from the real filing. Designed to test that a same-industry retrieval (Apple vs Microsoft, near-identical risk-factor boilerplate) attributes this correctly to Apple and not Microsoft.

questions.question: According to Microsoft's fiscal year 2023 Form 10-K, Item 1A Risk Factors, what does it say about competitive pressure in its markets?
questions.expected_answer: NEEDS VERIFICATION: could not retrieve the exact wording (the file is ~10MB and the fetch tool could not reach Item 1A). Open the downloaded MSFT_FY2023_10K yourself, find the Item 1A competition language, and fill in the exact quote and page before using this question.
questions.note: FLAGGED, not fabricated. Fill in after you open the real file. Pairs with Q11 as the other half of the same-industry collision test.

questions.question: What was Apple's operating income specifically for fiscal year 2022 (not fiscal year 2023)?
questions.note: tests year-confusion: the corpus has two Apple filings, this checks the system doesn't accidentally return the FY2023 figure instead

questions.question: What was Microsoft's revenue specifically for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2022 (not 2023)?
questions.note: same year-confusion test as Q13, for the other same-industry company

questions.question: Comparing Apple's fiscal year 2022 and fiscal year 2023 10-Ks, did net income increase or decrease, and by roughly how much?
questions.expected_answer: Decreased, from $99,803 million to $96,995 million, a decline of about $2,808 million (approximately 2.8%)
questions.source_section: Item 8, Consolidated Statements of Operations in both filings

questions.question: Between Apple's and Microsoft's fiscal year 2023 10-Ks, which company reported the higher operating margin?
questions.expected_answer: Microsoft (approximately 41.8%) reported a higher operating margin than Apple (approximately 29.8%)
questions.source_section: Item 8 income statement tables in both filings
questions.note: the flagship boilerplate-collision / metadata-filtering test question: needs correct company attribution across two same-industry filings

questions.question: Comparing Walmart's fiscal year 2022 and fiscal year 2023 10-Ks, did net income increase or decrease?
questions.expected_answer: Decreased, from $13,673 million to $11,680 million (a decline of about 14.6%)
questions.source_section: Item 8, Consolidated Statements of Income in both filings

questions.question: Comparing JPMorgan Chase's fiscal year 2022 and fiscal year 2023 10-Ks, what was the dollar change in net income?
questions.expected_answer: Increased by approximately $11,876 million, from $37,676 million to $49,552 million (about 31.5% growth)
questions.source_section: Item 8, Consolidated Statements of Income in both filings

questions.question: Across all four companies in the corpus, which one reported the highest net income in fiscal year 2023?
questions.expected_answer: Apple, at $96,995 million (vs. Microsoft $72,361M, JPMorgan $49,552M, Walmart $11,680M)
questions.source_section: Item 8 income statements across the corpus

questions.question: Which of the three non-financial companies in the corpus (Apple, Microsoft, Walmart) had the largest revenue in fiscal year 2023?
questions.expected_answer: Walmart, at $605,881 million net sales, far larger than Apple ($383,285M) or Microsoft ($211,915M)
questions.note: JPMorgan deliberately excluded from this one since banks report revenue on a fundamentally different basis (net interest income) that isn't apples-to-apples with product revenue

questions.question: What are the main risk themes that recur across the four companies' most recent (fiscal year 2023) 10-Ks?
questions.expected_answer: OPEN, deliberately hard: this is a synthesis question with no single supporting chunk. Fill in the real recurring themes (e.g. competition, regulation, cybersecurity, macroeconomic conditions) once you've actually read all four Item 1A sections. This question exists specifically to test whether the system falls into the 'retrieve 20 anecdotes, never synthesize' failure mode from the case-studies document.
questions.source_section: Item 1A, Risk Factors, across the corpus

questions.question: What is Apple's projected revenue for fiscal year 2026?
questions.note: 10-Ks report audited historical results, not forward projections; Apple also does not issue formal revenue guidance

questions.note: Tesla is not one of the four companies in this corpus
